raw_text:
Thanks — I’ll build a 12-week strength program for a 30‑year‑old advanced female lifter who is 20 weeks pregnant and cleared for moderate strength training. The plan respects pregnancy contraindications you listed: avoid supine exercise after week 16 (so no flat back lying work), avoid maximal efforts/near‑max attempts, avoid contact sports, and otherwise prioritize maternal/fetal safety, symptom monitoring, and pelvic floor and core support. Because she’s advanced we’ll keep intensity substantial but submaximal, with careful load management, slower progression, and substitution of safe positions.

Key assumptions and safety notes (please review with client):
- OB clearance for moderate strength training is in place. Trainer should monitor symptoms (dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, chest pain, vaginal bleeding, leakage of fluid, regular painful contractions, decreased fetal movement). Stop exercise and seek medical care if any occur.
- Avoid supine (flat) positions after week 16. Use upright, inclined, seated, or side‑lying alternatives.
- Avoid breath‑holding and Valsalva — cue controlled breathing and exhale during effort.
- No maximal 1RM testing. Use RPE and submaximal percentages. Aim for RPE 6–8/10 on working sets.
- Reduce impact and balance challenges as pregnancy progresses. Use support for single‑leg and unstable movements if needed.
- Keep hydration, avoid overheating; prioritize comfortable clothing and frequent rest.
- Emphasize pelvic floor awareness (gentle activation, avoid forcing kegels), and avoid exercises that provoke abdominal diastasis symptoms (coning, doming). If diastasis recti appears, adapt core work per pelvic floor/physio guidance.

Program overview
- Duration: 12 weeks. Client currently 20 weeks pregnant → program covers approx weeks 20–32 of pregnancy.
- Frequency: 3 strength sessions per week (full‑body focus), plus 1 optional light accessory/cardio/recovery session (walking, swimming, prenatal yoga) depending on energy and tolerance.
- Phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Maintain strength — moderate loading, focus on technique, pelvic floor, upper body & posterior chain. Loads ~70% of pre‑pregnancy working loads or RPE 6–7.
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength maintenance & controlled hypertrophy — slightly reduce load intensity frequency of heavier sets; prioritize single‑leg and core/postural control. Loads RPE 6–7. Reduce eccentric speed if needed.
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Transition to lower intensity, durability, and mobility — focus on safe range of motion, joint comfort, higher repetition conditioning, and preparation for late pregnancy. RPE 5–7.
- Session split: Push / Pull / Lower + posterior chain emphasis across three workouts per week; each session has primary movement(s), accessory work, core/pelvic floor emphasis, and mobility/finisher.

Progression and load prescription
- Use RPE 6–8 for primary lifts (no testing to failure). For an advanced lifter this might be roughly 70–80% of typical working loads but keep sets submaximal and add rest between sets.
- Progress by small increments (2.5–5% or by 1–3 reps) every 1–2 weeks as tolerated. If any exercise causes symptoms (pain, coning, leakage), regress or substitute.
- Reassess weekly via subjective readiness; reduce load on “bad” days.

Equipment options
- Barbells, dumbbells, kettlebells, trap bar/horizontal handles, cable machines, band resistance, adjustable benches set to incline, step/box, stability ball used upright only, and machines for supported squats/row variations. Avoid flat bench for supine work; use seated or inclined variants.

Detailed 12‑week plan (week‑by‑week structure)
Notes common to every session:
- Warm up (10–12 minutes): 5–8 minutes easy cardio (walking, cycling), dynamic mobility (hip circles, thoracic rotations, band pull‑aparts), activation (glute bridges on incline/standing banded mini‑band walks), pelvic floor cueing (gentle diaphragmatic breathing + pelvic floor awareness 1–2 sets of 8–10 reps).
- Breathing: inhale eccentrically, exhale concentrically. Avoid breath holding.
- Cool down: 5–10 minutes gentle mobility and stretching, rehydration, post‑session pelvic floor check (gentle diaphragmatic breathing).

Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4 (maintain strength; client weeks 20–24)
Goal: Maintain major strength and technical positions; posterior chain and upper body. RPE 6–7. 3 sessions/wk.

Week 1 (Intro)
Session A — Lower‑bias (posterior chain)
1) Trap bar deadlift or hex‑bar DL — 4 sets x 5 reps @ RPE 7 (submaximal; rest 2–3 min)
2) Bulgarian split squat (rear foot elevated on box, front foot supported if balance needed) — 3 x 8 each leg
3) Romanian deadlift with dumbbells — 3 x 8
4) Standing banded glute bridge (band around knees, standing leaning to bench) or glute bridge on incline bench if comfortable (avoid flat supine) — 3 x 12
5) Farmer carry (dumbbells) — 3 x 30–45s walks
Core/PG (pelvic floor): Standing anti‑extension plank into wall or incline plank — 3 x 20–30s, plus 1 set gentle pelvic floor activation x 8

Session B — Push‑dominant (upper)
1) Seated incline barbell or dumbbell press (back supported upright/incline) — 4 x 6–8 @ RPE 7
2) Single‑arm cable or dumbbell row (standing or chest‑supported incline on bench) — 3 x 8 each
3) Seated machine shoulder press (neutral grip if more comfortable) — 3 x 8
4) Banded chest press / cable press — 3 x 12
5) Triceps overhead cable or seated dumbbell triceps extension — 3 x 10
Core/PG: Modified side plank (on knees or elevated) 3 x 20–30s per side; gentle pelvic floor breathing work 1 x 8–10

Session C — Pull + single‑leg emphasis
1) Single‑leg Romanian deadlift (dumbbell) — 4 x 6–8 each leg (use support for balance)
2) Seated cable row or chest‑supported row — 4 x 6–8
3) Lat pulldown (kneeling or seated) — 3 x 8–10
4) Hip thrust variation using bench/incline support with band and light load (consider supported hip thrust where torso is on bench but feet stable — avoid lying flat unsupported) — 3 x 10
5) Banded monster walks — 3 x 15 each direction
Core/PG: Bird‑dog (kneeling) 3 x 8–10 each side; focus on neutral spine and pelvic floor activation.

Weeks 2–4
- Keep same structure. Small progressions: add 1–2 reps per set or +2.5–5% load if RPE <7 and client feels good. Maintain rest 90–180s for primary lifts. Maintain pelvic floor and diastasis monitoring. Add one optional light conditioning session (20–30 min walk or pool session).

Phase 2 — Weeks 5–8 (weeks 25–28 of pregnancy)
Goal: Maintain strength, add controlled volume and single‑leg work. Slightly reduce absolute loads as body changes; RPE 6–7. Continue 3 sessions/wk.

Week 5 (transition)
Session A — Lower
1) Goblet squat or belt squat (if available) — 4 x 6–8 (avoid deep breath holds; squats within comfortable ROM)
2) Trap bar deadlift — 3 x 5 (moderate)
3) Reverse lunge to box (split stance) — 3 x 8 each leg
4) Seated or standing calf raises — 3 x 12–15
5) Heavy carries (suitcase or farmer) — 3 x 30–45s
Core/PG: Seated pelvic tilts + gentle transversus abdominis draw‑in (not forced crunch) — 3 x 8–10; side‑lying clamshells 3 x 15

Session B — Upper push/pull mixed
1) Seated incline dumbbell press — 4 x 6–8
2) Single‑arm chest supported row or one‑arm dumbbell row (bench supported) — 4 x 8 each
3) Cable face pulls — 3 x 12–15
4) Banded pull‑downs or assisted pull‑ups — 3 x 6–8
5) Biceps curl superset triceps press — 3 x 10 each
Core/PG: Standing anti‑rotation press (pallof press, cable or band) 3 x 8 each side

Session C — Posterior chain & conditioning
1) Romanian deadlift light–moderate — 4 x 8
2) Step‑ups to bench (controlled) — 3 x 8 each leg
3) Hip hinge with banded walkouts or eccentric glute bridge (on incline) — 3 x 10
4) TRX rows (standing) — 3 x 10–12
5) Low‑impact interval cardio: 8–10 rounds of 30s moderate effort / 60s easy on bike or row (if comfortable)
Core/PG: Quadruped breathing (4‑point breathing) with bird‑dog 3 x 8 each

Weeks 6–8
- Continue similar template. Introduce slight variety (e.g., swap goblet for short bar squat, swap trap bar DL for sumo DL) but keep loads submaximal. Progress by reps or small load increases only if no symptoms. Reduce single‑leg difficulty if balance worsens (use support). Continue one recovery session/week: pool walking, prenatal yoga, or easy walk 20–40 min.

Phase 3 — Weeks 9–12 (weeks 29–32 of pregnancy)
Goal: Transition to durability, mobility and comfort, maintain joint integrity and posterior chain, reduce heavy loads. RPE ~5–7. 3 sessions/wk; more emphasis on higher reps and tempo control.

Week 9
Session A — Strength maintenance, lower emphasis
1) Belt squat or box squat (to a box at a comfortable depth) — 4 x 6
2) Romanian deadlift (lighter) — 3 x 8
3) Reverse lunge to support (hold rack/strap) — 3 x 8 each
4) Banded glute bridge on incline or standing band hip extension — 3 x 12–15
Core/PG: Standing pelvic floor and breathing drills; heel slides (supine avoided if after week 16; use incline or semi‑reclined) — 2 x 10

Session B — Upper
1) Seated machine chest press — 4 x 8
2) Seated cable row — 3 x 8–10
3) Dumbbell lateral raise seated — 3 x 12
4) TRX or band assisted pull‑downs — 3 x 10
5) Light farmer carries or suitcase walks — 3 x 40s
Core/PG: Pallof press 3 x 10 each side; side‑lying clamshells 3 x 15

Session C — Conditioning + mobility
1) Kettlebell deadlift / suitcase squat (light) alternating circuits: 4 rounds — 8 deadlifts + 8 goblet squats + 30s banded monster walk
2) Step ups or gentle stair climbing — 3 x 8 each
3) Seated row (high reps) — 3 x 12
4) Low impact steady state cardio 20–30 min (walking, bike) at comfortable effort
Core/PG: Quadruped pelvic tilts, pelvic floor coordination 3 x 10

Weeks 10–12
- Reduce heavy joint loading and maintain movement quality. Keep sets moderate (3–4) and reps 8–15. Prioritize rest and symptom monitoring. By week 32, expect decreasing tolerance for heavier sets — shift further to machines, single‑leg support and high‑rep lighter work if needed.

Optional modifications for symptoms or comfort changes
- If dizziness/lightheadedness: stop, sit, cool down, check hydration and blood sugar.
- If diastasis or bulging/coning: reduce or stop any exercises that provoke it. Switch core work to gentle transversus abdominis activation, side planks from knees, heel slides in semi‑reclined position, avoid full sit‑ups/crunches and heavy loaded carries until evaluated by physio.
- If balance is reduced: perform single‑leg movements with support or replace with double‑leg variations.
- If heart rate tolerance changes: use RPE rather than HR zones.

Nutrition and recovery guidance (pregnancy‑specific)
- Maintain a calorie intake sufficient for pregnancy + activity. General guidance: additional ~300 kcal/day in 2nd and 3rd trimesters, but adjust for pre‑pregnancy BMI and clinician advice.
- Protein: 1.1–1.3 g/kg/day or roughly 20–30 g high‑quality protein per meal/snack to support maternal and fetal tissue and maintain lean mass; for an advanced lifter, aim at the higher end (1.2–1.6 g/kg) if cleared by OB/dietician.
- Hydration: encourage drinking before, during and after sessions; avoid overheating. Electrolyte intake as needed.
- Micronutrients: prenatal vitamin as prescribed, adequate iron and folate per OB advice.
- Sleep: prioritize 7–9 hours where possible; naps as needed.
- Recovery: 1–2 rest days per week; active recovery like walking or swimming. Use contrast showers, manual therapy, and gentle stretching for soreness. Continue pelvic floor and breathing work daily (short sessions).

Sample weekly schedule (example)
- Monday: Session A (Lower)
- Tuesday: Recovery/optional light walk or prenatal yoga
- Wednesday: Session B (Upper)
- Thursday: Light pool session or rest
- Friday: Session C (Pull/posterior + conditioning)
- Saturday: Optional short walk/active recovery
- Sunday: Rest

Testing and load tracking
- No 1RM or maximal testing. Track RPE, sets/reps, and subjective readiness. Adjust loads conservatively. Consider auto‑regulation: if RPE >8 on planned working sets, reduce load 5–10% or reduce set count.

Additional cues for trainer
- Keep exercises upright or inclined rather than flat supine. When client needs back support, use an incline bench or seated machine.
- Encourage breath control and pelvic floor coordination; avoid forcing pelvic floor contractions between sets — encourage normal relaxed breathing and gentle activation.
- Encourage communication about fetal movement changes and any troubling symptoms.

If you’d like, I can:
- Convert this into a printable week‑by‑week table for the client,
- Provide a list of exact progressions (loads/percentages) based on her current working numbers,
- Or create a prenatal core progression sheet that you can hand to a pelvic health physio for review.

Which would you prefer next?
